answers.quote: India can be divided into the following physiographic divisions: (1) The Northern and North-eastern Mountains (2) The Northern Plain (3) The Peninsular Plateau (4) The Indian Desert (5) The Coastal Plains (6) The Islands.
answers.notes: c04 lists six physiographic divisions.

answers.quote: The approximate length of the Great Himalayan range, also known as the central axial range, is 2,500 km from east to west, and their width varies between 160-400 km from north to south.
answers.notes: c06 gives Great Himalayan range length ~2,500 km.

answers.quote: Bhabar is a narrow belt ranging between 8-10 km parallel to the Shiwalik foothills
answers.notes: c08 defines Bhabar belt at Shiwalik foothills where streams deposit boulders/disappear.

answers.quote: a belt consisting of old and new alluvial deposits known as the Bhangar and Khadar respectively
answers.notes: c10: old=Bhangar, new=Khadar (respectively).

answers.quote: 'Anaimudi' (2,695 m), the highest peak of Peninsular plateau is located on the Anaimalai hills of the Western Ghats followed by Dodabetta (2,637 m) on the Nilgiri hills.
answers.notes: c14: Anaimudi highest peak of Peninsular plateau.

answers.quote: They are separated by a waterbody which is called the Ten degree channel. ... Barren island, the only active volcano in India is also situated in the Andaman and Nicobar islands.
